21742-jarwin-and-cuffy:
A lovely, empty Pacific island opens this Ballantyne tale, rich with coconut palms, breadfruit, and birds, but with no sign of man. The fruit hangs ripe with no one to eat it. Then the story brings its castaways to that shore. Jarwin and Cuffy, the pair of the title, face the island together, one a man and one a boy in Ballantyne's world of castaway tales.

Adrift on the ocean first, they must learn the island's gifts and dangers to live. Ballantyne loved island stories above all, and he stocks this one with fish, storms, and strange visitors. It is a compact tale of survival, friendship, and making a home where no home was.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-sir-charles-g:
Charles Gavan Duffy, politician and author born at Monaghan, Ireland, on 12 April 1816, died at Nice, France, on 9 February 1903. Schooled in his home town, he wrote young for the Northern Herald and joined Dublin's Morning Register staff in 1836. In 1839 he became editor of the new Ulster Catholic paper, the Vindicator, at Belfast until 1842. Going to Dublin that summer, he met Thomas Davis and John Dillon, and with them founded The Nation.

Duffy edited the paper, and its fresh, vigorous, and militant tone soon made it a power. Wholehearted support of Repeal filled the association's coffers, and O'Connell gratefully acknowledged its help. When O'Connell was prosecuted in 1844, Duffy stood with him in the dock and shared his Kilmainham imprisonment. Later he sided with Young Ireland against O'Connell and helped found the Irish Confederation. Historical works, including Young Ireland and My Life in Two Hemispheres, crown his later career.
doe-osti-3016954-jupiter-laser-facility-:
Shelby Conn compiled the Jupiter Laser Facility annual report for fiscal year 2025, LLNL-TR-2015329, issued February 2026. The Jupiter Laser Facility at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory gives outside researchers access to high-power lasers for plasma and high energy density science. The report opens with a welcome letter from the facility director and a month-by-month set of highlights.

Inside, experiment summaries show the range of work the lasers support. One feature explains black hole accretion disk modeling, where matching observations takes more iron in the model than expected. Other sections track facility operations, user projects, and staff news across the year. For scientists considering beam time, and for funders checking what the facility produced, the annual report is the record of a working user facility in 2025.

podcast-dannyjones-_o9gpIa_qFY:
Mike Clelland joins Danny Jones to map a strange link between owls and UFO contact. People who report close contact often report owls at odd hours, and Clelland has spent years on that pattern. He calls it a screen that hides the real event.

Clelland shares case after case in which an owl shows up near a sighting or a lost block of time. He asks why the mind might swap a bird for a being. Jones draws out the best tales and the doubt that comes with them. Listeners get one of the oddest corners of UFO lore, told by its top collector.
podcast-dannyjones-a1kespVSrfY:
Attorney Danny Sheehan joins Danny Jones for a talk on aliens, false stories, and a secret state within the state. The episode title bills Sheehan as Harvard's UFO lawyer. He has worked big public cases for decades and now works on UFO law.

Sheehan tells what he says he saw in classified files and what he thinks the state still hides. He argues that lies planted in the press have kept the public in the dark. Jones asks what proof can be shown in court. Listeners get a lawyer's take on the UFO file. The library holds it as an archive record, without a side taken.
podcast-joerogan-NSFaaq3vhfY:
Filmmaker Dan Farah joins the Joe Rogan Experience for episode 2416 to discuss his UFO disclosure documentary. Farah gathered on-camera statements from officials and pilots for a film meant to push the subject into the open. Rogan's show is a natural stop for such a project.

Farah tells Rogan who agreed to speak, what they said, and what he left on the cutting floor. Rogan asks how a filmmaker checks claims that come from inside secret programs. The episode works as a behind-the-scenes record of disclosure as media strategy, and of the moment when UFO talk moved from podcasts to Congress and back.
podcast-tuckercarlson-mdvqSncd4FY:
Tucker Carlson and writer Michael Shellenberger team up to break down the California fires. Shellenberger is an author who writes on energy, land, and state policy. The two men argue the fires were made far worse by bad rule.

They walk through dry brush, cut funds, and laws that blocked clearing near homes. They blame state leaders for chasing green goals while towns burned. Carlson asks what a sane policy would look like. Listeners get a full case on the fires from two sharp critics. The library keeps the talk as a record of their stated view.
